findings.explanation: Cereal-based premix preparation: the documents contain contradictory information (95 kg (BOM), 3 bags (DOC-SUP-X1)). The result depends on this ingredient. The tool cannot use the value until the SME clarifies it.
findings.fix: Ask the SME which document is correct.

requirements.requirement: The product is in HS heading 19.01.
requirements.evidence: The declared HS code is 1901.10. The product description fits heading 19.01: “Infant cereal (precooked millet and soya with milk powder), for infants and young children, 400 g cartons”.

requirements.requirement: Imported ingredients of heading 19.01 are at most 15% of the ex-works price.
requirements.evidence: Cereal-based premix preparation may be an imported ingredient of heading 19.01. The value, HS code or origin is missing or contradictory. The share cannot be calculated yet.

requirements.requirement: The work done in Ghana includes eligible manufacturing processes under AfCFTA guidelines, not only mixing, grinding or packing.
requirements.evidence: These manufacturing processes are eligible under AfCFTA guidelines: roasting of millet and soya, cooking by extrusion and drum drying of the cooked paste.

requirements.requirement: No ingredient comes from food aid (donated or non-commercial supplies).
requirements.evidence: The production notes state that no ingredient comes from food aid.

requirements.requirement: There is proof of origin for local and AfCFTA ingredients.
requirements.evidence: Supplier declarations are on file for 3 of 3 ingredients from Ghana or other AfCFTA countries.
